check.reason: The target is right (pharma marketing), and the piece doesn't mock patients, authors or individuals, so it is satirical and on-target. The problem is the line 'Few interventions in medicine show such a clean dose-response relationship.' The summary only says gifts and payments increase inappropriate prescribing and likely raise costs. It says nothing about a dose-response finding, so this reads as a specific result the story doesn't support. Remove or soften it, for example: 'Few interventions in medicine are so consistently effective,' and it can pass.

pick.title: Pharma’s free lunches for doctors boost inappropriate prescribing, analysis finds
pick.headline: Study Finds Catered Lunch Remains Pharma's Most Cost-Effective Prescribing Intervention
pick.take: A new review finds that gifts and payments from drugmakers increase inappropriate prescribing, likely driving up costs. Few interventions in medicine show such a clean dose-response relationship. The sandwich was never the point, but it is still the only part of the educational program that reliably gets attended.
